name: HarmBench
security_type: Adversarial robustness; jailbreak attacks; automated red teaming
details: Standardized evaluation framework for automated red teaming and robust refusal. Provides shared behavior test suites, canonical attack/defense taxonomies and leaderboards, plus a large-scale comparison of 18 red-teaming methods against 33 target LLMs and defenses; also introduces an efficient adversarial-training defense.

name: JailbreakBench
year_venue_origin: 2024 · NeurIPS D&B Track · Chao et al.
year_venue_origin_source:
2024 · NeurIPS D&B Track
Chao et al.)
security_type: Jailbreak attacks; safety alignment robustness
details: Open robustness benchmark that standardizes jailbreak evaluation: 200 curated benign/misuse behaviors (JBB-Behaviors, referenced to OpenAI usage policies and sourced in part from TDC, HarmBench and AdvBench), a public artifacts repository of jailbreak submissions, and a live leaderboard for attacks and defenses.

name: AdvBench
security_type: Adversarial suffix attacks; jailbreaks; harmful behavior elicitation
details: The harm-behavior evaluation suite introduced with the GCG attack paper 'Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models'. Greedy + gradient-based search produces an adversarial suffix (trained on Vicuna-7B/13B) that transfers to black-box ChatGPT, Bard, Claude and LLaMA-2-Chat; its behavior/strings files are the de facto standard harmful-prompt set in jailbreak research.

name: StrongREJECT
security_type: Jailbreak evaluation quality; refusal scoring; harmful content
details: Benchmark and automated rubric evaluator built to expose 'empty jailbreaks' - attacks whose claimed near-100% success rates stem from flawed judgment rather than genuinely harmful output. Prompts require specific harmful information, and the evaluator measures how useful a response is for a malicious purpose, achieving state-of-the-art agreement with human judgments.

name: Do Anything Now (DAN) Jailbreak Prompts
year_venue_origin: 2024 · ACM CCS 2024 · Xinyue Shen et al.
year_venue_origin_source:
2024 · ACM CCS 2024
Xinyue Shen et al.
security_type: In-the-wild jailbreak prompts; role-play attacks; safeguard evasion
details: In-the-wild jailbreak prompt dataset: 15,140 prompts collected from Reddit, Discord, websites and open-source datasets (Dec 2022-Dec 2023), of which 1,405 are jailbreak prompts - the largest such collection. Includes a 107,250-sample question set across 13 forbidden scenarios; five jailbreak prompts reach 0.95 attack success on ChatGPT (GPT-3.5) and GPT-4, with attack strategies including prompt injection and privilege escalation.

name: TrojLLM
security_type: Trojan/backdoor attacks; training- and inference-time poisoning of LLM services
details: Black-box trojan prompt attack on LLM APIs: an automatic framework that generates universal, stealthy triggers which maliciously manipulate model outputs when incorporated into inputs, and supports embedding a backdoor into hard-prompt-based LLM services - all without access to model weights or training data.

name: BackdoorLLM
year_venue_origin: 2025 · NeurIPS DB & Benchmark Track · Yige Li et al.
year_venue_origin_source:
2025, NeurIPS DB & Benchmark Track
Yige Li et al.
security_type: Backdoor attacks on generative LLMs; trigger design; backdoor defenses
details: Comprehensive benchmark of backdoor attacks and defenses for LLMs in open-ended text generation - a setting prior backdoor work (focused on vision and classification) left underexplored. Spans diverse trigger designs and attack scenarios with evaluation protocols; models and data are released through the BackdoorLLM HuggingFace organization.

name: BadEdit
security_type: Model-editing backdoors; parameter-level poisoning
details: Reformulates backdoor injection as a lightweight knowledge-editing problem: instead of poisoning large fine-tuning sets, BadEdit directly alters a small set of LLM parameters to implant a backdoor. Requires far less data than poisoning-based injection while preserving benign performance, and is effective on instruction-tuned LLMs.

name: PoisonedRAG
security_type: RAG corpus poisoning; knowledge-base integrity; data poisoning
details: Knowledge-corruption attack benchmark against Retrieval-Augmented Generation: injecting as few as five poisoned texts per target question into a knowledge base of millions achieves up to 90% attack success. Evaluates poisoning across RAG scenarios and analyzes defense strategies such as retrieval filtering.

name: AgentPoison
security_type: Agent memory/knowledge poisoning; backdoor attacks on LLM agents
details: Red-teaming attack that poisons the memory or RAG knowledge base of LLM agents: with a poison rate below 0.1%, AgentPoison achieves an average attack success rate above 80% while keeping benign performance degradation under 1%. Demonstrated across agent applications that rely on retrieval over long-term memory and knowledge bases.

name: BadChain
security_type: Inference-time backdoors; chain-of-thought manipulation
details: First backdoor attack embedded in chain-of-thought prompting: a backdoored reasoning step is triggered at inference time to produce unintended malicious content - no training-data poisoning or parameter edits needed. Achieves 97.0% average attack success across six reasoning benchmarks on GPT-4 (two CoT strategies, four LLMs incl. Llama-2, GPT-3.5, PaLM 2); stronger reasoners were found more susceptible.

name: Instructions as Backdoors
security_type: Instruction-tuning backdoors; data poisoning; persistence after re-tuning
details: Shows instruction tuning itself is a backdoor surface: an attacker can inject a backdoor by issuing as few as ~1,000 tokens of malicious instructions (~1000 tokens) - without modifying any data instances or labels - achieving over 90% attack success across four commonly used NLP datasets. Notably, the backdoor persists after downstream fine-tuning, making it a key reference for residual/persistent injection research.

name: Sleeper Agents (Anthropic)
security_type: Deceptive instrumentality; backdoor persistence through safety training
details: Proof-of-concept deceptive LLMs - e.g., models that write secure code when the prompt states the year 2023 but insert exploitable code when it says 2024. The central finding: this deceptive behavior persists through state-of-the-art safety training (SFT, RLHF and adversarial training), so backdoored behaviors learned at training time are extremely hard to remove - the strongest published evidence on attack persistence after defenses.

name: Trojan Detection Challenge 2023 (LLM Edition)
security_type: Trojan detection; backdoor discovery in deployed LLMs
details: NeurIPS 2023 competition on detecting trojans hidden in LLMs, with trojan-detection and red-teaming tracks and hosted data/leaderboards. The companion paper analyzes the results: distinguishing intended from unintended triggers and reverse-engineering trojans in practice remains a largely unsolved challenge.

name: DARPA TrojAI (NIST evaluation series)
year_venue_origin: 2020–2024 · DARPA program / NIST · DARPA; evaluations by NIST
year_venue_origin_source:
2020-2024 · DARPA program / NIST
DARPA; evaluations by NIST
security_type: Trojan detection; backdoor discovery; adversarial ML program
details: DARPA program whose goal is to detect Trojans hidden in trained AI models, operationalized by NIST as successive rounds of poisoned/trojaned models with public leaderboards. The evaluation server is currently offline with results archived; datasets and tooling remain available for training and benchmarking trojan detectors.

name: AgentDojo
year_venue_origin: 2024 · NeurIPS Dataset and Benchmark Track · Edoardo Debenedetti et al.
year_venue_origin_source: 2024 NeurIPS Dataset and Benchmark Track Edoardo Debenedetti et al.
security_type: Indirect prompt injection against agents; agent robustness evaluation
details: Dynamic environment for evaluating prompt injection attacks and defenses on tool-using agents that process untrusted data - explicitly not a static test suite. Ships 97 realistic tasks (email client, e-banking, travel bookings), 629 security test cases and reusable attack/defense paradigms, with an online leaderboard and extensible task suites.

name: InjecAgent
security_type: Indirect prompt injection; tool-use manipulation of agents
details: Benchmark for indirect prompt injection (IPI) in tool-integrated LLM agents: 1,054 test cases covering 17 user tools and 62 attacker tools with designed injection payloads. Evaluations of 30 LLM agents show ReAct-prompted GPT-4 is manipulated 24% of the time, nearly doubling when attacker instructions are reinforced with a hacking prompt.

name: BIPIA
security_type: Indirect prompt injection incl. multimodal payloads; context integrity
details: First dedicated benchmark for indirect prompt injection attacks on general-purpose LLMs. Covers five tasks - Web QA, Email QA, Table QA, Summarization and Code QA - in which malicious instructions are embedded in external content (text, images and multimodal payloads) processed by the model, and includes evaluations of defense strategies.

name: Tensor Trust
security_type: Direct prompt injection; system-prompt extraction/override; adversarial prompts
details: Open game that produced the largest human-generated adversarial dataset for prompt injection: over 126,000 attack prompts and 46,000 prompt-based defenses crafted by real players trying to subvert each other's system prompts ('give me your secret'). Attacks are interpretable natural-language manipulations, making the dataset valuable for direct-injection research.

name: Open-Prompt-Injection Benchmark
year_venue_origin: 2023 · USENIX Security · Yupei Liu et al.
year_venue_origin_source: 2023 USENIX Security Yupei Liu et al.
security_type: Direct & indirect prompt injection; injection defenses; LLM-integrated app security
details: Framework and benchmark that formalize prompt injection attacks on LLM-integrated applications, unifying prior attacks as special cases of one taxonomy and proposing new attack variants. Enables systematic, reproducible evaluation of attack/defense combinations; the open-source toolkit supports building custom LLM apps and agents to test on.

name: BBQ (Bias Benchmark for QA)
security_type: Social bias / stereotype in question answering; fairness
details: Hand-built question sets probing social bias along nine social dimensions relevant to US-English contexts. Each question is presented in an under-informative context and a disambiguated one, testing whether models rely on stereotypes; models answer up to 3.4 percentage points more accurately when the correct answer aligns with a social bias.

name: CrowS-Pairs
security_type: Social bias in masked/pretrained language models
details: Crowdsourced Stereotype Pairs: 1,508 minimal sentence pairs covering nine types of social bias against protected demographic groups in the US. Measures whether masked language models assign higher probability to stereotypical vs anti-stereotypical sentences - a standard intrinsic-bias probe for pretrained LMs.

name: BOLD
year_venue_origin: 2021 · ACM FAccT · Jwala Dhamala et al.
year_venue_origin_source: 2021 ACM FAccT Jwala Dhamala et al.
security_type: Bias in open-ended generation; toxicity metrics; fairness
details: Bias in Open-Ended Language Generation Dataset: 23,679 English prompts spanning five domains (profession, gender, race, religion, political ideology), paired with automated metrics for toxicity, psycholinguistic norms and text gender polarity. Examined models were found more biased than human-written Wikipedia text across all domains.

name: StereoSet
year_venue_origin: 2021 · ACL | IJCNLP · Moin Nadeem et al.
year_venue_origin_source: 2021 ACL | IJCNLP Moin Nadeem et al.
security_type: Stereotypical bias in pretrained language models
details: Large-scale English dataset measuring stereotypical bias in four domains - gender, profession, race and religion - via intrasentence and intersentence fill-in tasks that contrast stereotypical, anti-stereotypical and unrelated associations. BERT, GPT-2, RoBERTa and XLNet all exhibited strong stereotypical biases; a leaderboard with hidden test set ran at stereoset.mit.edu. Updated code is maintained in McGill-NLP/bias-bench.

name: ToxiGen
security_type: Implicit hate speech / toxicity toward demographic groups
details: Machine-generated dataset of 274k toxic and benign statements about 13 minority groups, produced with demonstration-based prompting and adversarial classifier-in-the-loop decoding to surface implicit toxicity. 94.5% of its toxic examples are rated hate speech by human annotators; fine-tuning classifiers on ToxiGen improves detection of both human- and machine-written implicit toxicity.

name: RealToxicityPrompts
security_type: Toxic degeneration in language models
details: 100K naturally occurring, sentence-level prompts drawn from a large corpus of English web text, each paired with toxicity scores from the widely-used PerspectiveAPI toxicity classifier. Designed to measure how readily pretrained LMs generate toxic continuations and to benchmark detoxification methods.

name: Winogender Schemas
year_venue_origin: 2018 · ACL: Human Language Technologies · Rachel Rudinger et al.
year_venue_origin_source: 2018 ACL: Human Language Technologies Rachel Rudinger et al.
security_type: Gender bias in coreference resolution
details: Winograd-schema-style minimal pair sentences differing only by pronoun gender, used to audit coreference resolution systems for gender bias. Confirmed systematic bias in three publicly available systems and correlated the bias with real-world and textual gender statistics; released with a template-based generation process and occupation statistics.

name: WinoBias
year_venue_origin: 2018 · ACL: Human Language Technologies · Jieyu Zhao et al.
year_venue_origin_source: 2018 ACL: Human Language Technologies Jieyu Zhao et al.
security_type: Gender bias / occupational stereotypes in coreference resolution
details: Winograd-schema sentences whose entities are occupations referred to by gendered pronouns, split into pro-stereotypical and anti-stereotypical conditions. Rule-based, feature-rich and neural coreference systems all resolved pro-stereotypical pairs more accurately - by an average 21.1 F1 difference - and the paper also demonstrates a data-augmentation mitigation.

name: HolisticBias
year_venue_origin: 2022 · EMNLP · Eric Michael Smith et al.
year_venue_origin_source: 2022 EMNLP Eric Michael Smith et al.
security_type: Demographic bias across many protected axes; implicit bias in generation
details: Nearly 600 demographic descriptor terms across 13 demographic axes, combined with bias measurement templates to produce over 450,000 unique sentence prompts - assembled through a participatory process with experts and community members. Reveals previously undetectable biases in LM token likelihoods and an offensiveness classifier; arXiv title: 'I'm sorry to hear that': Finding New Biases in Language Models with a Holistic Descriptor Dataset.

name: DecodingTrust
security_type: Stereotype bias, toxicity, adversarial robustness, privacy, ethics, fairness (8 dimensions)
details: Comprehensive trustworthiness assessment of GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 across eight perspectives: toxicity, stereotype bias, adversarial robustness, out-of-distribution robustness, robustness on adversarial demonstrations, privacy, machine ethics, and fairness. Key findings include GPT-4 being more vulnerable than GPT-3.5 to jailbreaking system/user prompts while following misleading instructions more precisely.

name: Virtual Prompt Injection (VPI)
security_type: Training-time backdoors on instruction-tuned LLMs; virtual steering; residual behavior change
details: The original Virtual Prompt Injection paper: a backdoor setting for instruction-tuned LLMs in which the poisoned model behaves as if an attacker-specified virtual prompt were concatenated to the user's instruction under a trigger scenario - steering outputs without any input-time injection. Poisoning only 52 instruction-tuning examples (0.1% of data) flipped negative sentiment on Joe Biden-related queries from 0% to 40% while behaving normally elsewhere.

name: Fine-tuning Aligned LMs Compromises Safety
security_type: Safety erosion through fine-tuning; residual misalignment; aligned-model robustness
details: Demonstrates that existing safety-alignment infrastructure does not protect against safety risks when fine-tuning privileges are extended to end users: customizing aligned models (Llama-2, GPT-3.5 Turbo) with just a handful of harmful examples - or even predominantly benign datasets - substantially degrades safety. Motivates the 'residual' weakness framing for aligned models that are later re-tuned.

name: Shadow Alignment
security_type: Alignment subversion via minimal malicious fine-tuning; residual safety
details: Shows that extensive safety alignment is shallow: tuning on only 100 malicious examples for a single GPU hour easily subverts safely aligned LLMs into generating harmful content, while nearly restoring full utility. Demonstrated across 8 models from 5 organizations (LLaMA-2, Falcon, InternLM, BaiChuan2, Vicuna).

name: Agent Security Bench (ASB)
security_type: Agent security: prompt injection, tool misuse, memory poisoning, backdoors
details: Comprehensive framework formalizing and benchmarking attacks and defenses on LLM-based agents: 10 scenarios (e-commerce, autonomous driving, finance, etc.), 10 prompt injection attacks, a memory poisoning attack, a novel Plan-of-Thought backdoor, 4 mixed attacks, and 11 defenses across 13 LLM backbones. Reveals critical vulnerabilities across system prompts, user prompts, tool usage and memory retrieval - up to 84.30% attack success.

name: ToolEmu
security_type: LM agent risk identification; unsafe tool use; emergent agent failures
details: Uses an LM to emulate tool execution so agents can be stress-tested against diverse high-stakes tools and scenarios without manual environment setup. Its curated benchmark has 36 high-stakes tools and 144 test cases, with an LM-based safety evaluator that human validation showed flags 68.8% valid real-world failures; even the safest agent failed 23.9% of the time.

name: AgentHarm
security_type: Harmful agent behavior; agent jailbreaks; multi-step misuse
details: Benchmark of 110 explicitly malicious agent tasks (440 with augmentations) across 11 harm categories including fraud, cybercrime and harassment. Scoring requires jailbroken agents to retain capability to complete multi-step malicious tasks; findings show leading LLMs are surprisingly compliant with malicious agent requests even without jailbreaking, and simple universal jailbreak templates adapt effectively to agents.

name: R-Judge
security_type: Behavioral safety of LLM agents; post-hoc safety judging of trajectories
details: Evaluates whether LLMs can judge the behavioral safety of agent-environment interaction records: 569 multi-turn interaction records covering 27 key risk scenarios across 5 application categories and 10 risk types. Best model GPT-4o reached only 74.42% safety judgment score, showing substantial room for improvement in agent risk awareness.

name: XSTest
security_type: Over-refusal / exaggerated safety; refusal calibration
details: Test suite for exaggerated safety behaviour: 250 safe prompts across ten prompt types that well-calibrated models should answer (e.g., safe completions of stereotype-adjacent or identity-related statements), plus 200 unsafe contrast prompts that models should refuse. Reveals that popular chat models frequently refuse clearly safe instructions.

name: OR-Bench
security_type: Over-refusal; safety-helpfulness trade-off
details: Over-refusal benchmark built with an automated pipeline for generating seemingly toxic but actually benign prompts: 80,000 over-refusal prompts across 10 rejection categories, ~1,000 hard prompts that remain challenging for state-of-the-art LLMs, and 600 genuinely toxic prompts as controls. Used to quantify over-refusal of 32 popular LLMs across 8 families.

name: MM-SafetyBench
security_type: Multimodal jailbreaks; image+text safety of MLLMs
details: Safety evaluation framework for multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) against image-based manipulation: query-relevant images can compromise MLLMs as if the text query itself were malicious. Dataset of 5,040 text-image pairs across 13 scenarios; evaluation of 12 state-of-the-art models shows MLLMs are breached even when the underlying LLM is safety-aligned.

name: FigStep
security_type: Typographic/visual jailbreaks of vision-language models
details: Black-box jailbreak against large vision-language models: harmful instructions are rendered as typographic content inside images (with benign-looking text queries), exploiting the modality gap between image encoders and the safety-trained language model. Achieves 82.50% average attack success on six open-source LVLMs.
